analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Tech Colour / Metals & Mining (I) / Europe Banks / VAT / Ericsson 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities fell on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 posting its first -1% move in 53 days: SPX -111bps to 7718, NDX -202bps to 29,950, RTY -193bps to 2729. 8 of 11 sectors fell, with a rotation into defensives (Tech -2.62%, Communication Services -1.73%, Healthcare +2.44%, Staples +2.38%).
Markets now price a 35% probability of a Fed hike in October and 87% for December. GIR continues to expect a second hike in December.
GS custom baskets showed a flight to safety: Global NeoClouds (GSXGNEOC) -10.93%, GS Quantum Computing index (GSX1QNT1) -7.14%, Expensive Defensive (GSXUEDEF) +1.18%.
European equities closed higher (SXXP +40bps, SX5E +40bps) with a defensive tilt: Healthcare (SXDP) +2.3%, Food & Bev (SX3P) +1.4%, Personal Goods (SXQP) +1.6%.
Options markets continue to price considerable dispersion through year-end during 3Q earnings season. 3-month implied correlation is below the 2nd percentile of the last twenty years.

Global fundamental long/short hedge funds fell 0.8% (-1.7 standard deviations), mainly from beta. They are down 2% month to date and up 10.6% year to date. TMT-focused funds fell 2.7% on the day, down 4.5% month to date and up 13% year to date.

Tech selloff drivers (NDX -2%): credit-market concern about the ability to keep financing the AI trade, neocloud weakness (-12%, a top-5 move in the past 5 years) and hyperscaler bond yields, plus a hotter-than-expected CPI (core 33bps vs consensus 20bps, from firmer shelter). Other concerns cited: OpenAI revenue confusion, Chinese memory breakthroughs easing bottlenecks, datacenter sentiment into midterms, future power/shell constraints and further issuance.
Upcoming catalysts: PPI report and Warsh's speech in Bangkok.

Metals & Mining initiation: Buy on Endeavour Mining (12m TP GBP47/sh) and AngloGold Ashanti (12m TP $104/sh), Neutral on Gold Fields (12m TP $38/sh). EDV has the strongest mix of organic growth and FCF yield. AGA has operational consistency, a capital-efficient brownfield pipeline and the highest prospective shareholder returns, with Nevada as longer-term optionality. GFI's medium-term growth increasingly depends on Windfall, and Tarkwa risk and Australian cost pressure add uncertainty.

Europe Banks: most constructive on BNP, BCP, BBVA, SocGen, Intesa, ING, STAN and Erste into the quarter. Consensus expects sector aggregate ROTE of 15.4% (+1.4ppt y/y) and PBT up 16%. GS sees upside risk from higher interest rate expectations not fully reflected in consensus.

Nordea reported results in line at every P&L line and on CET1. The buyback is paused pending clarification of REA impact from non-retail capital models. Consensus has E250m of buybacks in Q4 and E850m in 2027, and removing them would be about a 2% negative EPS impact and about 70bps of capital relief.

EQT: AuM of 194.8 includes 34bn from Coller. Excluding that, gross inflow was E8bn vs consensus 12.3bn. EQT XI was delayed and Infra VII is expected around year end. Exits were E3bn in the quarter and 10bn year to date, against an expectation similar to last year's E20bn, which may be hard to reach.

VAT Group (Buy, PT CHF782, 25% upside): 3Q26 orders beat company-compiled consensus by 40%, order growth rate of 188% is the highest ever and book-to-bill is 1.9x, also a record. Consensus FY27 EPS is likely to rise by a low double-digit percentage. Management expects strong investment conditions into 2027 and beyond, and 2027 guidance is now expected significantly above the prior CHF1.5-1.7bn range (consensus CHF1.9bn, GSe CHF2.1bn, 14% above consensus).

Ericsson Q3 beat: revenue SEK59.48bn, 7% ahead, driven by Networks (Asia, Oceania and India beat while Americas declined). Gross margin was 8% ahead and EBITA beat by 28% at SEK10.12bn vs 7.93bn expected (margin 17% vs 14.3% Street). It was a consensus short, and shares were up 3% on Tradegate on low volume.

market_movers.rationale: Endeavour Mining offers the strongest combination of organic growth and FCF yield, backed by sector-leading production growth.
AngloGold Ashanti offers operational consistency, a capital-efficient brownfield pipeline and the highest prospective shareholder returns in GS gold coverage, with Nevada as longer-term optionality.
Gold Fields has a high-quality, diversified asset base, but medium-term growth depends increasingly on Windfall, and Tarkwa risk and Australian cost pressure add uncertainty.
VAT Group posted a 40% orders beat, record order growth of 188% and book-to-bill of 1.9x. 2027 guidance is expected well above the prior CHF1.5-1.7bn range, with GSe at CHF2.1bn.
Q3 revenue, gross margin and EBITA all beat, with better cost control. The stock was a consensus short, so GS expects a positive reaction and relative outperformance.

sector_views.rationale: Consensus expects Q3 aggregate ROTE of 15.4% and PBT up 16%, and higher rate expectations are not fully reflected in consensus. Most constructive on BNP, BCP, BBVA, SocGen, Intesa, ING, STAN and Erste.
Buy ratings on Endeavour and AngloGold Ashanti and Neutral on Gold Fields, initiated on growth, FCF yield and shareholder returns.
Flight to safety saw Healthcare and Staples lead in the US and Europe while Tech and NeoClouds sold off.

VAT Group 3Q26 (reported): orders beat company-compiled consensus by 40%, order growth was 188% and book-to-bill was 1.9x. 2027 guidance is expected significantly above the prior CHF1.5-1.7bn (consensus estimate CHF1.9bn, GSe CHF2.1bn).
Ericsson Q3 (reported): revenue SEK59.48bn, 7% ahead of consensus. EBITA was SEK10.12bn vs SEK7.93bn expected, a 28% beat. EBITA margin was 17% vs Street estimate 14.3%. Gross margin was 8% ahead.
